analyst_view.overall: Hearts (32nd of 36, 1 point) host Monaco (4th, 9 points from 9) at a sold-out Tynecastle; Hearts have not won in nine European games this season and need points, while Monaco are almost through. Hearts arrive after an 8-0 win at Dundee, with Borchgrevink, Mato and Ageu back and Vrancken expected to make few changes, but nine players including McEntee, Fagan-Walcott, Kingsley, Halkett and Spittal are out, all in the numbers (including a big cut for McEntee). Monaco miss Golovin, Ansu Fati and Idumbo (counted), with Christian Mawissa doubtful with a groin problem; Paris Brunner (four goals in the competition) and Balogun are expected to lead the attack. Austrian referee Daniel Schlager, around average at 4.1 cards a game, is already counted. Nothing new is big enough to move the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, 2.3 for Monaco, and already take big cuts for Hearts without McEntee and for Monaco without Golovin and Idumbo. Monaco's expected front two of Brunner and Balogun is close to full strength, and Hearts' big win at Dundee came against weak opposition, so I stay at 3.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.3 corners, nearly even, as Hearts tend to go direct and win set pieces at home while Monaco keep the ball. Nothing in the team news changes that, so I stay at 10.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards and already count referee Daniel Schlager, close to the average at 4.1 a game over 37 games. A loud Tynecastle and a Hearts side chasing the game could add a booking, but that is a hunch, so I stay at 3.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.9 shots. Hearts are expected to keep a similar eleven and Monaco to field Brunner and Balogun up front despite their absences, so I see no reason to move from 25.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target, 5.1 for Monaco. The absences that matter on both sides are already counted and Mawissa's doubt is in defence, so I stay at 8.8.
